أَكْيَاتٌ i. q. أَكْيَاسٌ, [pl. of كَيِّسٌ:] (K:) the Rájiz says, “غَيْر أَعِفَّاءِ وَلَا أَكْيَاتِ
” [Not such as abstain from things unlawful and unbecoming, nor ingenious, or acute in mind, &c.]. (TA.) See art. س p. 1281 a. Some say, that it it is a word mispronounced: others, that it is formed by the change of س into ت, as in the case of طَسٌّ and طَسْتٌ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
